summary: Nix research program phases 4+5 for one wave: sonnet deep dives per commissioned subtopic, pipelined into one opus consolidation (or revision) per group
logs: Wave 3: 6 dives across 3 groups (inputsx2, packagingx2, releasex2); revising: none
Wave 3 done: 3/3 groups consolidated · 21 MUST rules · 36 surprises · 13 follow-ups

top_rules: Decide follows by how the input is consumed (cache-package: never; library/module/overlay: yes or take pkgs as arg; generated-flake FOD-only input: irrelevant) — the Nix manual itself says a sub-flake's own nixpkgs is 'usually irrelevant'

jq '[.nodes[] | select((.original.type=="github") and (.original.repo=="nixpkgs"))] | length' flake.lock — count must be 1 (or 0), never treat 4 identical-content nixpkgs nodes as fine: Nix never dedups by content, only by follows

Pin every input's own transitive nixpkgs to a 40-hex sha, never a floating branch ref, closing #14339's actual blast radius (removing follows re-resolves a floating ref fresh, not the dependency's own committed lock)
Never assume plain `nix flake lock` refreshes a path: input after editing its target dir — it silently kept a stale narHash in a fixture; only `nix flake update <name>` picked up the change

Run flake-checker advisory-only with CEL `supportedRefs.contains(gitRef) && numDaysOld < 30 && owner == 'NixOS'` under --fail-mode, and split its crash (stderr Error: Invalid(/FlakeLock() from a real finding — never a MUST gate
Trust the installed flake-checker binary's own supported-branch list over its README: 0.2.15 flagged nixos-25.11 as unsupported even though its own main-branch README already lists it

In a generated flake's FOD+wrapper shape, follows never changes the FOD's outPath, only the wrapper's drvPath — verified, but only after discarding a false-positive first attempt (pkgs.hello.src changes across nixpkgs revisions because hello's own version bumped, not because of follows)
NixOS/nix#5393's self-follow segfault is fixed on 2.35.2 — a genuine follow cycle now fails cleanly with 'error: follow cycle detected: [...]', exit 1; stop citing the segfault as current
surprises: NixOS/nix#5393 (self-follow segfault) does not reproduce on Nix 2.35.2 — it's now a clean 'follow cycle detected' error, exit 1

#14339 (removed follows ignores dependency's own lock) only manifests when the dependency's own input is a floating branch ref; with a full-sha pin, plain `nix flake lock` correctly restored the exact original pin
A local path: input is NOT auto-refreshed by plain `nix flake lock` after its content changes on disk — the lock silently kept the old narHash until `nix flake update <name>` was run explicitly
flake-checker 0.2.15's compiled-in supported-branch list is stricter than its own README fetched fresh from main the same day (binary omits nixos-25.11, README already lists it)

Even three inputs pinned to the byte-identical nixpkgs revision produce 4 separate nixpkgs-shaped lock nodes with no follows — Nix's lock never dedups by content, confirmed both by fixture and by a NixOS Discourse thread

First attempt at the FOD+wrapper fixture gave a false positive: using pkgs.hello.src as the 'FOD' showed different outPaths across nixpkgs revisions purely because nixpkgs bumped hello's own version between 25.11 and 26.11pre, not because of follows

top_rules: Never use channels.nixos.org/.../nixexprs.tar.xz (dead after 2027-12-31); use github:, git+https: or same-tree path:./sub only
Declare inputs.self.submodules=true — without it, consumers silently get an empty submodule dir that throws far from the input declaration
Declare inputs.self.lfs=true, but test it only against a real http(s) LFS remote — Nix's LFS client rejects file:// with 'uploading to ... is not supported'
Monorepos split via same-tree path:./sub only; cross-repo path:../sibling is illegal by design on every Nix version tested (error text changed 2.20.6→2.31.5/2.35.2, same illegality)
A cross-repo sibling input needs an absolute path: or git+file:?rev=<sha> — both verified clean on 2.35.2
Read locked.type not original.type for an indirect input — today it resolves to a tarball node against releases.nixos.org, not github
Never rely on nixConfig.warn-dirty=false — verified inert without accept-flake-config, matching open NixOS/nix#9885

CI eval-budget gates need wall-clock timeout AND a stage-line-progress check — nix-installer/treefmt-nix hang silently at the same 300s ceiling that helix's legitimate 303-grammar network fetch also hits
surprises: Helix's "~100 tree-sitter inputs" are not flake.nix inputs at all — they're 303 builtins.fetchTree calls inside grammars.nix driven by languages.toml, invisible to any inputs/flake.lock scan; a more general and harder-to-spot risk than the brief's framing implied

The cross-repo path:../sibling error message changed between Nix versions: 2.20.6 said 'points outside of its parent's store path'; 2.31.5/2.35.2 both say 'access to absolute path ... forbidden in pure evaluation mode' — same illegal shape, different diagnostic text, so a grep-the-error-string diagnose rule silently stops firing on current Nix

inputs.self.lfs=true does real work (confirmed by its own 'smudging git-lfs file' trace) but Nix's LFS client only speaks HTTP(S) batch — a file:// remote fails distinctly even with the object already present locally, so a local-mirror CI test gives false confidence
nixConfig.warn-dirty=false is a complete no-op without accept-flake-config, confirmed directly — matches an open issue since Nix 2.18.1, still unfixed
An indirect nixpkgs input resolves to a tarball-type locked node against releases.nixos.org today, not a github node — original.type tells you nothing about the real fetch path

Monorepo flake layering is not an unsettled documentation gap but genuinely unsettled community practice as of mid-2026 — the cited live Discourse thread's top answer is essentially 'hire a consultant'

rule_ids: NIX-INP-01 — Decide follows by how the input is consumed: follow for library, module or overlay inputs, never for inputs you want cached packages from (with a comment saying why); keep Q1-transitive empty or justified
NIX-INP-02 — Give a library or module flake a root with zero inputs or only nixpkgs-lib; put test and dev inputs in a test/ sub-flake driven by --override-input
NIX-INP-03 — Name a branch or tag in each input url and let flake.lock carry the rev; put a 40-hex rev in url only for inputs frozen on purpose, with a comment
NIX-INP-04 — Commit no local inputs (absolute path:, git+file:, or path:../ outside the tree) in a published lock; allow only same-tree path:./sub (Nix >=2.26)
NIX-INP-05 — Give every input an explicit scheme (github:, git+https:, or channels .tar.zst); never use a bare registry name, nixexprs.tar.xz, or a FlakeHub input in fleet flakes
NIX-INP-06 — Track a nixpkgs branch the installed flake-checker binary supports, keep it under 30 days old, and check with the CEL condition under --fail-mode as an advisory step
NIX-INP-07 — Move lock entries with nix flake update <input> (including edited path: inputs); never use --update-input or --recreate-lock-file
NIX-INP-08 — After any follows edit, re-lock and read the lock diff; after removing a follows, check the dependency's nixpkgs rev against the dependency's own lock
NIX-INP-09 — Declare inputs.self.submodules and inputs.self.lfs in the publisher's flake.nix instead of relying on ?submodules=1; test LFS over an https remote
NIX-INP-10 — Keep builtins.fetchTree, fetchGit, fetchTarball and fetchurl unreachable from outputs; use a locked flake = false input or a pkgs.fetch* fixed-output derivation instead
NIX-INP-11 — Refresh the lock weekly with a scheduled, SHA-pinned workflow that opens a PR (never a push) under an App or fine-grained token so the gate runs
NIX-INP-12 — Consider an --override-input nixpkgs-unstable CI leg for flakes others consume as inputs; never commit the override
conflicts_resolved: Q1 duplicate-nixpkgs filter: the map's and the follows dive's filters both miss FlakeHub and channel tarball nixpkgs (0 reported for 5 corpus flakes that carry one; nix-installer 2 vs 4). Replaced by Q1-transitive, which matches on repo, id or url and lists only transitive nodes. This also reconciles shape §2 and runs Axis 1.

--update-input: the map said it was gone since 2.19. Measured: a deprecated alias on CppNix 2.31.5 and 2.35.2 (exit 0 with a warning), a hard error on Lix 2.95.2 (exit 1). It stays a MUST on the Lix-leg evidence.
#5393 follow-cycle segfault: the map treated it as a live guard, the dive as fixed. Measured: a clean error on CppNix 2.31.5 and 2.35.2, a stack overflow on Lix 2.95.2.
The follows dive's rule 3 (40-hex rev in every url) is rejected. A rev in url makes nix flake update a silent no-op (measured). Branch in url, lock as the pin.
The input-types dive's cross-repo fix (absolute path: or git+file:?rev) is local-dev-only via --override-input; a committed published lock must never hold it.

helix '~100 flake=false inputs' (map M-B-08, runs smell 6) vs shape §2 (2 inputs, 0 flake=false): the cost is 303 eval-time builtins.fetchTree calls in grammars.nix, so the rule targets eval-time fetchers.
update-flake-lock README (@main, Determinate installer, personal token) vs NIX-GATE-12/13 and NIX-GEN-16: SHA-pinned, CppNix installer, App or fine-grained token.
flake-checker README vs binary branch list: the binary wins (0.2.15 rejects nixos-25.11).
Follows-as-hygiene (H2) vs the manual and nixpkgs-python: kept map conflict 3's resolution, made concrete as a consumption table plus a justification comment.
needs_another_round: checks-ci eval budget: does a 60 s no-new-stage-line watchdog on nix flake check --no-build -v separate helix-style fetch fan-out from nix-installer/treefmt-nix hangs, measured cold?

inputs-lock lazy fetching: under CppNix 2.35 lazy copies, does an unaccessed transitive lock node (nix-installer's nixpkgs-regression) cost consumers a fetch or only lock bytes? This decides whether NIX-INP-02 becomes MUST.
inputs-lock #14339: re-derive the floating-ref removed-follows drift and check that the --override-input restore is exact.
inputs-lock self.lfs: does it work over a real HTTPS LFS remote, and how do CppNix 2.31.5 and Lix 2.95.2 handle inputs.self.lfs and submodules?
impls Lix follows: track the stack overflow on a follow cycle and the proposal to drop follows (M-B-13) across Lix releases.

top_rules: Never write cargoLock.lockFile = "${src}/Cargo.lock"; use ./Cargo.lock instead — the interpolated form is red on a cold store, green only on a warm one (verified exit 1 vs 0)
Never write src = builtins.path { path = self; } (the exact flake-checker.nix:193 idiom) — same eval-time-read cold failure, reproduced for crane specifically (exit 1 vs 0)

grimoire's real packaging blocker is git submodules (docker_credential, rust-oci-client), not -sys crates: fetchGit's default submodules=false resolves them to empty dirs, breaking even local `nix build .`

buildRustPackage never reads rust-toolchain.toml; pin the exact channel via rust-bin.fromRustupToolchainFile (rust-overlay) if the flake claims to match `cargo build` — verified this pinned build compiles grimoire successfully
aws-lc-sys (the fleet's one shared hard native dep, pulled in transitively via rustls) builds clean under buildRustPackage with only pkg-config in nativeBuildInputs — verified by a real nix build
clang-sys in ocx's lock is aws-lc-sys's own optional bindgen build-dep (traced via cargo tree --target all -i clang-sys), inactive on Linux glibc/musl targets — not a mystery transitive dependency

Neither buildRustPackage, crane, nor buildPythonPackage trips the 'system'-has-been-renamed warning under --all-systems (count 0 in all three) — wave 2's 56-warning case is nix-installer's own expression, not a builder property

ocx-sdk-python needs plain buildPythonPackage{pyproject=true}, not uv2nix — zero runtime deps means no dependency graph for uv2nix to translate; verified by a full nix build reaching pythonMetadataCheckPhase
surprises: The brief's framing of "crane's measured red case" (flake-checker) is wrong at the mechanism level: it's not crane vs buildRustPackage, it's the `src = builtins.path { path = self; }` eval-time self-read idiom — reproducible identically with buildRustPackage

grimoire's git submodules (docker_credential, rust-oci-client forks) resolve to EMPTY directories under Nix's default fetchGit submodules=false, breaking cargo with a plain 'No such file or directory' error that never mentions Nix or submodules — and this breaks even a local `nix build .` inside the checked-out repo, not just remote/CI fetches

A first build attempt produced a false alarm: nixpkgs' rustc (1.98.1) appeared to break grimoire's compile with real type errors, suggesting a toolchain-version regression — retracted after finding the actual cause was this dive's own `rsync --exclude=catalog` deleting src/catalog/ (matched both the intended top-level docs dir and the real source subdir)

aws-lc-sys compiled with zero extra native inputs beyond pkg-config despite the build log showing 'Compiling cmake v0.1.58' as a dependency — the crate's own README says CMake is 'never required' for non-FIPS, and no cmake binary was ever added to nativeBuildInputs, yet the build succeeded (mechanism left unresolved, flagged in Contested/evolving)

clang-sys in ocx's Cargo.lock is NOT in the activated dependency graph at all for the host platform (`cargo tree -i clang-sys` prints 'nothing to print'); it only shows up with `--target all`, meaning lock-file presence is not evidence of an active build requirement

cargoLock with explicit cargoToml/cargoLock over crane's cleanCargoSource ./. behaves identically (cold-safe) to the bare form — the brief's 'with and without explicit cargoToml/cargoLock' permutation makes no measurable difference

top_rules: Use mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {...}), never rec, for any package needing self-reference — a rec copy of the finalAttrs idiom hard-errors 'undefined variable finalPackage'.
src = lib.fileset.toSource {root; fileset;}, never ./. or self unfiltered — naive src changes drvPath on any unrelated edit (watched red), fileset src stays byte-identical.
Every package sets meta.description/license/mainProgram/platforms; shape D additionally sets meta.sourceProvenance — a single jq predicate catches any missing field, watched red on 4 planted twins.

Never hand-write a fetcher hash: use one of the four blessed placeholders (lib.fakeHash/fakeSha256/fakeSha512/"") — any other wrong hash silently degrades the fetch to curl --insecure, an MITM exposure.
Every overridden phase must open/close with runHook pre/postX — omitting it builds fine but silently drops any postInstall a downstream overrideAttrs adds (confirmed: MARKER file absent vs present).
substituteInPlace must use --replace-fail, never bare --replace — the bare form still silently exits 0 on a non-matching pattern on nixpkgs 26.11pre (nixpkgs#356002 still open).
strictDeps=true demands build tools in nativeBuildInputs, not buildInputs — misplacement fails at build time with an exact 'command not found' from stdenv's setup script.

__structuredAttrs's env attrset never accepts lists (regardless of the flag); its real payoff is a plain top-level list attribute surviving as a real bash array instead of being space-joined then word-split (measured: wrong count 3 vs correct count 2).
surprises: lib.fileset.toSource reads through its own filtered store path (readFile "${src}/Cargo.lock") did NOT trigger NIX-FLK-07's cold-store failure — toSource's add-to-store happens synchronously at eval time, unlike reading a real build output; the two rules address different objects, not a contradiction.

A 7-hex short rev against fetchFromGitHub built successfully in this environment — the short-rev danger is fork/rename-ambiguity-dependent, not a deterministic build failure, so it stays a reading heuristic, not a gate.
lib.fakeHash is literally the string sha256-AAAA...AAA= (32 zero bytes, SRI-encoded) — a hand-typed all-A hash and pkgs.lib.fakeHash produced byte-identical drvPaths and error messages.

__structuredAttrs does NOT loosen the env attrset's type rules — env forbids list values with or without __structuredAttrs; the real fix is for plain top-level list attributes, which only survive as real bash arrays (not space-joined then word-split) once __structuredAttrs is on.

The legacy sha256 = "..." fetcher attribute name still builds successfully on nixpkgs 26.11pre — it's a pure style/deprecation finding, never a build failure, contrary to a plausible assumption that it was hard-removed.
substituteInPlace's bare --replace still silently exits 0 with no visible warning on a non-matching pattern (nixpkgs#356002 opened 2024-11-14 is still open, unresolved as of 2026-09-27).

rule_ids: NIX-PKG-01 — Fetch src with a nixpkgs fetcher and SRI `hash =`; never builtins fetchers, `sha256 =`, cargoSha256 or vendorSha256 (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-02 — Pin with a full 40-hex `rev` or a real `tag`; never a short or truncated hex, a branch, or `tag = "<hex>"` (nurl 0.4.1 emits that for any non-40-hex argument) (MUST)
NIX-PKG-03 — Never hand-write a hash; use nurl/nix-prefetch or one of the four blessed fake hashes and copy `got:` (MUST)
NIX-PKG-04 — On any fetcher-argument change, reset the hash in the same edit and verify with `nix build --rebuild .#<pkg>.src`; a plain build reuses the old store path (MUST)
NIX-PKG-05 — Use `src = lib.fileset.toSource` over an explicit list; never unfiltered `./.` or `self`; never `gitTracked` inside a flake (MUST for A)
NIX-PKG-06 — Put `package.nix` at the repo root with nixpkgs-only formals and no `../`, so a by-name submission swaps only src, version and the cargo hash (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-07 — Set meta description (nixpkgs grammar), license, platforms and homepage; mainProgram per FLK-15/GEN-13, provenance per GEN-12 (MUST presence, SHOULD grammar)
NIX-PKG-08 — Never pass a compound SPDX expression to getLicenseFromSpdxId; CI evaluates with abort-on-warn (MUST)
NIX-PKG-09 — Put build tools in nativeBuildInputs and set `strictDeps = true` from the first commit (MUST)
NIX-PKG-10 — Set `__structuredAttrs = true`; keep `env` scalar and put lists at the top level (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-11 — Wrap every overridden phase in runHook pre/post; never set `phases` (MUST)
NIX-PKG-12 — Use `--replace-fail`/`--replace-warn`; never bare `--replace` in new code (MUST)
NIX-PKG-13 — Give every A CLI `versionCheckHook` with `doInstallCheck = true`; deeper behaviour goes in passthru.tests on finalAttrs.finalPackage (MUST for A CLIs)
NIX-PKG-14 — Use `finalAttrs:` only for self-reference, never `rec` for it; otherwise a plain attrset, because an unused finalAttrs fails deadnix (SHOULD)

NIX-PKG-15 — In-repo Rust uses buildRustPackage with `cargoLock.lockFile = ./Cargo.lock`; never `${src}/Cargo.lock` (even over a fileset) or `builtins.path { path = self; }`; cargoHash only for nixpkgs (MUST)
NIX-PKG-16 — Build with the pinned nixpkgs rustPlatform plus a floor check against the rust-toolchain.toml channel; no rust-overlay in package.nix (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-17 — Start native inputs at pkg-config and add only what an error names; trace -sys/bindgen with `cargo tree --target all -i` (SHOULD)
NIX-PKG-18 — Python uses buildPythonPackage with `pyproject = true` and the pyproject's own build-system; uv2nix only for compiled runtime deps (SHOULD)
conflicts_resolved: Short-rev 'did not go red': the dive's 'full 40-hex' baseline was 39 hex and every plain build was a store hit; a short rev resolves under --rebuild, so the rule stays and is enforced by a grep watched red/green (P3, P4)

The dive's 'fully gated' package.nix skeleton has `tag = <hex>` (copied from nurl) that 404s; it passed only because the store already held the output; superseded by a verified Rust template, and PKG-04 makes --rebuild mandatory (P2)

derivation-conventions' exemption for reads through a lib.fileset.toSource path is overturned: `${finalAttrs.src}/Cargo.lock` over a fileset is red cold (tarball) and locally; FLK-07 stands, and yazi is a violator (P10)
fleet-builders `src = ./.` vs derivation-conventions fileset: fileset wins, built and cold-checked with buildRustPackage (P9, P10)
fleet-builders 'pin via rust-overlay' rejected for stock rustPlatform plus a floor check (by-name readiness, consumer lock cost; the check went red/green, P11)

fleet-builders submodule fixes (flake inputs or ?submodules=1) vs NIX-INP-09: `inputs.self.submodules = true` wins; new measurements: Lix 2.95.2 needs flake-self-attrs, local CppNix fails with 'not tracked by Git' (P12)
finalAttrs-everywhere (map conflict 20) vs deadnix GATE-05: an unused finalAttrs fails deadnix, so it is for self-reference only, else a plain attrset (P9)
derivation-conventions' combined Q7 jq is constant-true (`or true`); replaced by a set-wide check red on 3 twins; mainProgram stays with FLK-15/GEN-13, provenance with GEN-12 (P8)
cargoHash vs cargoLock: cargoLock in-repo (rust.section.md:120-126), either in nixpkgs (:71); 'upstream as a copy' refined to a copy plus a three-attribute swap
fleet-builders 'build only nightly or on tag' vs NIX-GATE-10 MUST per-PR build: GATE-10 stands (no number was measured)
Legacy `sha256 =` demoted MUST to SHOULD (it builds); fleet-builders' `self + "/Cargo.lock"` alternative dropped (FLK-07 read-via-self was red)
needs_another_round: packaging/ocx-source-build — does ocx build end to end (workspace, cargoBuildFlags for the ocx bin crate, zstd-sys/liblzma-sys/libbz2-rs-sys vendored vs system, ocx_cli build.rs), what are its measured cold/warm wall times, and does a store cache make GATE-10's per-PR build affordable?

packaging/darwin-and-aarch64 (M-D-23) — do aws-lc-sys, security-framework-sys and core-foundation-sys build on aarch64-darwin (SDK 14.4 floor) and aarch64-linux with only pkg-config, on native runners?
packaging/python-library-export — should a Python library flake export via packages plus a pythonPackagesExtensions overlay or a top-level overlay attribute bound to one interpreter (NIX-FLK seam)?

inputs/self-submodules-remote — does inputs.self.submodules work when fetched as github:ocx-sh/grimoire/<rev> under the 2.31 floor, Lix with flake-self-attrs, and Determinate Nix (P12 was local only)?

top_rules: Read version via lib.importTOML on a self-tree path (./Cargo.toml); never src-interpolate a fetcher-backed src into that read — it forces derivation realization at eval time and goes red under `nix flake check --no-build --option allow-import-from-derivation false` (verified exit 0 vs 1)

Never embed revision in `version` to save rebuilds — moving rev into an env var does NOT reduce drvPath churn; only omitting self.rev entirely survives an unrelated commit (verified: baseline drvPath stable, both rev-carrying twins changed)

Always use `self.shortRev or self.dirtyShortRev or "unknown"` — `self.shortRev or "dirty"` silently discards the real hash on a dirty tree since shortRev is simply absent when dirty, not present-but-wrong
`path:` refs never carry git identity (rev/shortRev/revCount all MISSING, clean or dirty) — use `git+file:` for any local testing that needs real self.rev

`nix eval --json` on any self-shaped attrset (one with an outPath key) silently collapses to just that outPath string, discarding every sibling field — an undocumented trap for debug/CI scripts; use per-field access instead

A tagged release does not guarantee version equals the tag: sxyazi/yazi@0ea4c5d9ef75 at tag v26.9.1 reads Cargo.toml's clean 26.9.1 but ships packages.default.version = 26.9.1pre20260901_8dd895c because its snapshot suffix is unconditional — verified live against the real tag

FlakeHub stays unadopted (owner Q1): a rolling release (0.1.<commit-count>) is permanently shadowed by any real tag ≥0.2.0 under highest-semver-wins resolution — confirmed via imTHAI/nix-packages' own workflow comment describing exactly this failure and its fix

`nix-update -F --version=X` only rewrites what it can structurally trace from version: `rev` must be written as `finalAttrs`-interpolated (`"v${finalAttrs.version}"`), a bare literal or plain sibling reference is left untouched or hard-errors

A published flake's compatibility promise names a specific pinned CppNix version plus a relative floor (`nixVersions.nix_2_31` = 2.31.5 in the pinned channel) — RFC 136 permits breaking changes to flakes until an undated future stabilization, so never promise flakes themselves are stable

The lock is refreshed and gate-verified as its own commit before a release tag is cut, never regenerated as part of tagging; a shallow CI checkout is not dirty on 2.35.2 so no defensive fetch-depth gymnastics are needed
surprises: `nix eval --json` on any attrset carrying an `outPath` key (which `self` always has) collapses the entire serialized object to just that outPath string, silently discarding every sibling field — reproduced with a minimal non-flake expr, not previously documented anywhere in the map

A src-interpolated manifest read doesn't just fail on cold cache — under a plain `nix eval` (IFD allowed) it actively attempts a live network fetch to resolve `version`, and only errors cleanly when `allow-import-from-derivation` is explicitly disabled

Moving a commit revision from `version` into a separate env var does not reduce drvPath churn at all — both approaches force a rebuild on every commit including commits that touch nothing the package's filtered source includes; only omitting self.rev entirely is immune

sxyazi/yazi, a maintained and frequently cited-as-exemplary flake, ships a Nix `version` that differs from its own git tag even at the exact tagged commit, because its date+rev snapshot suffix is unconditional rather than gated on tag-vs-untagged

A GitHub archive tarball URL (with a visible commit SHA in the URL itself) gives strictly less self-metadata than the `github:` shorthand for the identical commit — no self.rev/shortRev at all, only lastModified(Date)

nix-update correctly discovered the true new hash for a version-bumped fetchFromGitHub source internally (replaying its own subprocess showed the correct sha256), but did not write that hash back to the fixture's package.nix in this nested-bwrap sandbox — flagged as an unresolved environment-vs-tool-limitation question rather than settled

top_rules: Cite NixOS/flake-compat only — nix-community's fork now self-declares unmaintained and redirects to it, overturning the topic map's open-choice framing (conflict 10).
lib.warn/builtins.warn fire on any evaluation of the wrapped attribute, including a plain `nix flake show` — verified live.

lib.derivations.warnOnInstantiate stays silent on `nix flake show` (unwraps meta/name/type) and only fires on an actual build or drvPath force — the two package-deprecation mechanisms are not interchangeable.
`nix flake check --no-build` still forces every package's drvPath ("checking derivation …"), so it fires warnOnInstantiate too, unlike `nix flake show` — verified live.

Never set `--option abort-on-warn true` on a CI gate step running `nix build`/`nix flake check` — it hard-fails those (exit 1, verified) but is silently swallowed by `nix flake show` (exit 0), an inconsistency that breaks CI the day any deprecation fires.
On Nix ≥2.23 (this program's floor is 2.31) `lib.warn` IS `builtins.warn` verbatim — not two mechanisms, one function with two call sites.

No public `nixConfig` substituter for fleet flakes by default (owner Q2); even the allowed keys are inert for a consumer without `accept-flake-config`, so any cache line must be documented as opt-in, never automatic.

Shape `package.nix` as `pkgs/by-name/<2-letter>/<name>/package.nix` from day one — nixpkgs's own docs state only PRs to that structure get self-service auto-merge, so retrofitting later is the costly path.
surprises: nix-community/flake-compat's own README (fetched live, 2026-09-27) declares the fork unmaintained and redirects to NixOS/flake-compat — the topic map's conflict 10 treated this as a live two-fork choice, but it had already collapsed to one canonical source by fetch time.

warnOnInstantiate and lib.warn diverge exactly at `nix flake show` (silent vs firing) but converge again at `nix flake check --no-build`, since that check forces drvPath per package — a subtler split than 'two interchangeable warn mechanisms'.

`--option abort-on-warn true` hard-fails `nix build`/`nix eval`/`nix flake check` but is silently swallowed by `nix flake show` (still exits 0) — `flake show` catches per-node eval errors internally for display, so it can't be used to sanity-check the gate's abort-on-warn behavior.

The audit's own README-install-hint numbers disagree internally (prose says 20 'no clear hint', the per-row table shows 17 dashes + 3 'overlay' rows = 20) — re-reading the 17 by hand found most are correctly hint-less (library flakes, template-init repos, external docs links), not README gaps at all.

A 5th, real install idiom (`nix shell <flakeref>#pkg`, used by cachix/nixpkgs-python) was missed entirely by the original audit's 4-pattern grep, as was the `nix flake init -t` template-init idiom used by crane/NixOS-templates/blueprint.
`edolstra/flake-compat` isn't a competing fork at all — it 301-redirects to the identical NixOS/flake-compat content, so citing it is stale-URL cosmetics, not a compatibility risk.

rule_ids: NIX-REL-01 — Read version from the manifest via lib.importTOML ./Cargo.toml or ./pyproject.toml; never a literal, never through ${src} (MUST)
NIX-REL-02 — Emit the manifest version verbatim with no pre/+rev/-dirty suffix, because self carries no tag (MUST)
NIX-REL-03 — Keep self.rev and its siblings out of exported derivations; if embedded, only outside version, accepting per-commit drvPath churn (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-04 — Read self metadata only as self.shortRev or self.dirtyShortRev or "unknown"; never expect rev under path: (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-05 — Ship default.nix and shell.nix through NixOS/flake-compat only, never edolstra or nix-community (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-06 — Take no FlakeHub input or publish step in fleet flakes; FlakeHub publishers use tagged releases only, never rolling after a >=0.2.0 tag (MUST fleet / SHOULD)
NIX-REL-07 — Release by the project's existing vX.Y.Z tags pinned as github:owner/repo/vX.Y.Z; a D flake's lock revision is its version (MUST)
NIX-REL-08 — Refresh flake.lock in its own commit before the release; the tag commit never touches flake.lock (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-09 — Give README install lines nix run, nix profile add with an install fallback for Lix, and an input snippet; never nix-env -i or --accept-flake-config (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-10 — Deprecate for one release before deletion: lib.warn, warnOnInstantiate, per-attribute tree warn, the FLK-04 shim, mkRenamedOptionModule for module options (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-11 — Never run abort-on-warn on nix flake check or a whole-flake build; apply it only to named current attributes (MUST)
NIX-REL-12 — State compatibility as the pinned CppNix, the GATE-16 computed floor, Lix advisory, and RFC 136 experimental; never 'works with Nix' (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-13 — Interpolate a fetcher ref from finalAttrs.version so nix-update -F moves version, rev and hash together (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-14 — Keep package.nix nixpkgs-ready; the upstream copy swaps only version, src and hash, adds updateScript or the opt-out, and uses the pkg: init at commit grammar (CONSIDER)
NIX-REL-15 — Stand up no public substituter (Q2); if one exists, document the nix.conf pair as an explicit opt-in (SHOULD)
NIX-REL-16 — Before announcing, run nix run github:owner/repo/vX.Y.Z -- --version from a clean store and require X.Y.Z in the output (MUST)
conflicts_resolved: Suffix at a tagged commit: the dive allowed a suffix except at a tag, yazi appends one always. Resolved: never add a suffix, because self exposes no tag or ref (C2 measured)
Revision placement: map conflict 8 put it in an env var; the dive measured that the env var churns the drvPath too. Resolved: the default package reads no revision (REL-03)

abort-on-warn: the map's wave-4 amendment and NIX-GEN-14 use it, the publishing dive banned it from CI. Resolved: allowed only on named current attributes; the scoped eval stayed green with a shim present while the whole-flake check went red (C4)
nix profile add vs install: the dive said never install, but Lix 2.95.2 rejects add (C3). Resolved: add is primary with an install fallback comment
flake-compat source: map conflict 10 and shape audit section 8 treated nix-community as live/maintained, but its README says unmaintained. Resolved: NixOS/flake-compat only
The fleet-builders dive hardcodes version literals 0.14.2 and 0.2.0. Resolved: REL-01 wins in-repo; a literal belongs only in the nixpkgs copy
'nixpkgs submission is a copy' vs a manifest-reading in-repo package.nix. Resolved: a copy plus a three-attribute swap, with package.nix at the repo root so PKG-01's no-../ check holds
Lock order at release was a reading heuristic. Resolved: made mechanical with git diff --quiet vX.Y.Z~1 vX.Y.Z -- flake.lock (C5)
README gap count 20 vs 17 in the shape audit. Resolved: the table's 17 is ground truth, and rules are conditioned on flake shape
follows line in the README snippet vs NIX-INP's consumed-as rule. Resolved: no follows by default, plus an optional line stating the trade-off

surprises: inputs/follows-and-lock-hygiene: NixOS/nix#5393 (self-follow segfault) does not reproduce on Nix 2.35.2 — it's now a clean 'follow cycle detected' error, exit 1

inputs/follows-and-lock-hygiene: #14339 (removed follows ignores dependency's own lock) only manifests when the dependency's own input is a floating branch ref; with a full-sha pin, plain `nix flake lock` correctly restored the exact original pin

inputs/follows-and-lock-hygiene: A local path: input is NOT auto-refreshed by plain `nix flake lock` after its content changes on disk — the lock silently kept the old narHash until `nix flake update <name>` was run explicitly

inputs/follows-and-lock-hygiene: flake-checker 0.2.15's compiled-in supported-branch list is stricter than its own README fetched fresh from main the same day (binary omits nixos-25.11, README already lists it)

inputs/follows-and-lock-hygiene: Even three inputs pinned to the byte-identical nixpkgs revision produce 4 separate nixpkgs-shaped lock nodes with no follows — Nix's lock never dedups by content, confirmed both by fixture and by a NixOS Discourse thread

inputs/follows-and-lock-hygiene: First attempt at the FOD+wrapper fixture gave a false positive: using pkgs.hello.src as the 'FOD' showed different outPaths across nixpkgs revisions purely because nixpkgs bumped hello's own version between 25.11 and 26.11pre, not because of follows

inputs/input-types-and-sources: Helix's "~100 tree-sitter inputs" are not flake.nix inputs at all — they're 303 builtins.fetchTree calls inside grammars.nix driven by languages.toml, invisible to any inputs/flake.lock scan; a more general and harder-to-spot risk than the brief's framing implied

inputs/input-types-and-sources: The cross-repo path:../sibling error message changed between Nix versions: 2.20.6 said 'points outside of its parent's store path'; 2.31.5/2.35.2 both say 'access to absolute path ... forbidden in pure evaluation mode' — same illegal shape, different diagnostic text, so a grep-the-error-string diagnose rule silently stops firing on current Nix

inputs/input-types-and-sources: inputs.self.lfs=true does real work (confirmed by its own 'smudging git-lfs file' trace) but Nix's LFS client only speaks HTTP(S) batch — a file:// remote fails distinctly even with the object already present locally, so a local-mirror CI test gives false confidence
inputs/input-types-and-sources: nixConfig.warn-dirty=false is a complete no-op without accept-flake-config, confirmed directly — matches an open issue since Nix 2.18.1, still unfixed

inputs/input-types-and-sources: An indirect nixpkgs input resolves to a tarball-type locked node against releases.nixos.org today, not a github node — original.type tells you nothing about the real fetch path

inputs/input-types-and-sources: Monorepo flake layering is not an unsettled documentation gap but genuinely unsettled community practice as of mid-2026 — the cited live Discourse thread's top answer is essentially 'hire a consultant'

packaging/fleet-builders: The brief's framing of "crane's measured red case" (flake-checker) is wrong at the mechanism level: it's not crane vs buildRustPackage, it's the `src = builtins.path { path = self; }` eval-time self-read idiom — reproducible identically with buildRustPackage

packaging/fleet-builders: grimoire's git submodules (docker_credential, rust-oci-client forks) resolve to EMPTY directories under Nix's default fetchGit submodules=false, breaking cargo with a plain 'No such file or directory' error that never mentions Nix or submodules — and this breaks even a local `nix build .` inside the checked-out repo, not just remote/CI fetches

packaging/fleet-builders: A first build attempt produced a false alarm: nixpkgs' rustc (1.98.1) appeared to break grimoire's compile with real type errors, suggesting a toolchain-version regression — retracted after finding the actual cause was this dive's own `rsync --exclude=catalog` deleting src/catalog/ (matched both the intended top-level docs dir and the real source subdir)

packaging/fleet-builders: aws-lc-sys compiled with zero extra native inputs beyond pkg-config despite the build log showing 'Compiling cmake v0.1.58' as a dependency — the crate's own README says CMake is 'never required' for non-FIPS, and no cmake binary was ever added to nativeBuildInputs, yet the build succeeded (mechanism left unresolved, flagged in Contested/evolving)

packaging/fleet-builders: clang-sys in ocx's Cargo.lock is NOT in the activated dependency graph at all for the host platform (`cargo tree -i clang-sys` prints 'nothing to print'); it only shows up with `--target all`, meaning lock-file presence is not evidence of an active build requirement

packaging/fleet-builders: cargoLock with explicit cargoToml/cargoLock over crane's cleanCargoSource ./. behaves identically (cold-safe) to the bare form — the brief's 'with and without explicit cargoToml/cargoLock' permutation makes no measurable difference

packaging/derivation-conventions: lib.fileset.toSource reads through its own filtered store path (readFile "${src}/Cargo.lock") did NOT trigger NIX-FLK-07's cold-store failure — toSource's add-to-store happens synchronously at eval time, unlike reading a real build output; the two rules address different objects, not a contradiction.

packaging/derivation-conventions: A 7-hex short rev against fetchFromGitHub built successfully in this environment — the short-rev danger is fork/rename-ambiguity-dependent, not a deterministic build failure, so it stays a reading heuristic, not a gate.

packaging/derivation-conventions: lib.fakeHash is literally the string sha256-AAAA...AAA= (32 zero bytes, SRI-encoded) — a hand-typed all-A hash and pkgs.lib.fakeHash produced byte-identical drvPaths and error messages.

packaging/derivation-conventions: __structuredAttrs does NOT loosen the env attrset's type rules — env forbids list values with or without __structuredAttrs; the real fix is for plain top-level list attributes, which only survive as real bash arrays (not space-joined then word-split) once __structuredAttrs is on.

packaging/derivation-conventions: The legacy sha256 = "..." fetcher attribute name still builds successfully on nixpkgs 26.11pre — it's a pure style/deprecation finding, never a build failure, contrary to a plausible assumption that it was hard-removed.

packaging/derivation-conventions: substituteInPlace's bare --replace still silently exits 0 with no visible warning on a non-matching pattern (nixpkgs#356002 opened 2024-11-14 is still open, unresolved as of 2026-09-27).

release/versioning-and-tags: `nix eval --json` on any attrset carrying an `outPath` key (which `self` always has) collapses the entire serialized object to just that outPath string, silently discarding every sibling field — reproduced with a minimal non-flake expr, not previously documented anywhere in the map

release/versioning-and-tags: A src-interpolated manifest read doesn't just fail on cold cache — under a plain `nix eval` (IFD allowed) it actively attempts a live network fetch to resolve `version`, and only errors cleanly when `allow-import-from-derivation` is explicitly disabled

release/versioning-and-tags: Moving a commit revision from `version` into a separate env var does not reduce drvPath churn at all — both approaches force a rebuild on every commit including commits that touch nothing the package's filtered source includes; only omitting self.rev entirely is immune

release/versioning-and-tags: sxyazi/yazi, a maintained and frequently cited-as-exemplary flake, ships a Nix `version` that differs from its own git tag even at the exact tagged commit, because its date+rev snapshot suffix is unconditional rather than gated on tag-vs-untagged

release/versioning-and-tags: A GitHub archive tarball URL (with a visible commit SHA in the URL itself) gives strictly less self-metadata than the `github:` shorthand for the identical commit — no self.rev/shortRev at all, only lastModified(Date)

release/versioning-and-tags: nix-update correctly discovered the true new hash for a version-bumped fetchFromGitHub source internally (replaying its own subprocess showed the correct sha256), but did not write that hash back to the fixture's package.nix in this nested-bwrap sandbox — flagged as an unresolved environment-vs-tool-limitation question rather than settled
